If it persists or worsens, a quick check-in with a dentist or oral surgeon could help confirm whether it’s muscle strain, TMJ irritation, or something else.

If it persists or worsens, a quick check-in with a dentist or oral surgeon could help confirm whether it’s muscle strain, TMJ irritation, or something else.
(c) It’s possible that the muscles and joint on that side are experiencing minor strain from overuse or an uneven bite, which can sometimes cause localized soreness when chewing. If it persists or worsens, a quick check-in with a dentist or oral surgeon could help confirm whether it’s muscle strain, TMJ irritation, or something else.
(d) It’s possible that the muscles and joint on that side are still a bit sensitive from when you had your impacted wisdom tooth removed — sometimes the bite mechanics shift slightly afterward, leading to localized soreness when chewing. If it persists or worsens, a quick check-in with a dentist or oral surgeon could help confirm whether it’s muscle strain, TMJ irritation, or something else.
